incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired for service=db-pool-acceptqueue at 2025-03-14T18:03:19Z - urgency=high - reason=pgbouncer accept queue > 2000 and api latency spike :rotating_light:
oncall-jordan: Acked. I'm on it, pulling logs and metrics now.
oncall-jordan: Quick snapshot from Grafana: pgbouncer_accept_queue ~2400, pg_active_conns ~1200, app error 503s ramping.
mira: I saw Redis errors in traces too; some pods reporting "ERR max number of clients reached". Could be simultaneous saturation of both caches and DB causing cascading backpressure.
alex: Jumping in, can we confirm which service is over-connecting? Probably model-metadata reads from Postgres on request path.
oncall-jordan: Running `psql -c "select state, count(*) from pg_stat_activity group by state;"` returned a ton of idle-in-transaction and active. Posting snippet:
```
active | 842
idle   | 276
idle in transaction | 312
```
We have a few long-running migrations? Not sure yet.
alex: Deploy logs show a cron job `model-sync` started 1m before spike, looks like it's retrying on failure and opening many connections.
```
2025-03-14T18:01:50Z model-sync[replica-3]: connection attempt failed, retrying
2025-03-14T18:02:05Z model-sync[replica-3]: opening pg connection
```
oncall-jordan: PagerDuty-bot: assign to oncall-jordan -> acknowledged.
pagerduty-bot: Incident assigned to oncall-jordan; if no ack in 5m will escalate.
liz-cs: Heads up, CS is seeing customer error reports for model lookups, some customers getting 503s in the last 3m. Impacting hosted API.
mira: Immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle model-sync (kill job) 2) increase pgbouncer replicas/allow more client connections 3) flip feature flag to bypass DB reads for non-critical endpoints.
oncall-jordan: I can kill the offending job first. Running `kubectl get pods -l app=model-sync -n jobs` then `kubectl delete pod model-sync-replica-3`
deploy-bot: Command accepted: deleting pod/model-sync-replica-3 - terminated.
oncall-jordan: Killed the runaway pod. Observing pg_active_conns drop from 1200 -> 680 over the next 30s. pgbouncer_accept_queue -> 400. API 503s decreased but still noisy.
alex: I'll scale pgbouncer replicas to buy time: `kubectl scale deployment pgbouncer -n infra --replicas=4`
deploy-bot: Scaling pgbouncer to 4 replicas.
mira: Can we temporarily increase pgbouncer `max_client_conn`? That requires config reload; if scaling buys time we can avoid restart.
oncall-jordan: Also enabling ingress rate-limit for model metadata endpoint to 10rps per IP to reduce thundering herd. Pushing config now.
alex: Adding read-replica routing for non-critical reads (bypass primary) via quick config flip. Pushing patch.
liz-cs: Customers asking ETA - what's safe to tell them?
mira: Tell them we're mitigating, dropping error rate, expect partial restoration within 5-10 minutes. We'll follow up if we need longer.
oncall-jordan: Current numbers: pgbouncer_accept_queue=120, pg_active_conns=420, redis_clients=~980 (maxclients=1024), API 503 rate down 85%.
pagerduty-bot: Oncall escalation: no further escalation required.
mira: We'll keep monitoring. Next actions: 1) audit model-sync retries and fail the job root cause 2) add circuit-breaker to metadata path 3) runbook update: mark model-sync job as critical to have backoff.
alex: I've submitted a short postmortem stub and a hotfix to disable model-sync auto-retry. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/model-sync/pull/482
oncall-jordan: Handoff to mira in 25min for post-incident follow-up. Leaving note: pgbouncer warmed up, no customer-facing errors for 10m.
liz-cs: Thanks team - CS will reply to incoming tickets with the update.
incident-bot: Incident resolved (no active pages) at 2025-03-14T18:15:10Z — duration ~12m  (runbook: db-connection-surge).
